Cross-platform parity: **11.7%**  
Status: **in progress**

The mobile tranche is implemented, documented, and source-matched to an installed Android release.

- [Build specification](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:75) now defines exact-model controls, typography parity, authenticated Courses behavior, consent, materials, and atomic Tutor handoff.
- [Execution plan and pseudocode](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430) records the checkpoint and prevents incomplete M3/M4 work from being counted.
- [Evidence baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:70) is synchronized.

Accepted:

- P0 and D1.
- Internal foundations D2a and M1a remain accepted but contribute no independent progress.

Verified:

- Mobile: 110 tests passing, 420 assertions.
- Strict TypeScript check passed.
- Android export: 2,005 modules, 36 assets, 5.5 MB Hermes bundle.
- Release APK: 100.1 MB, 946 Gradle tasks.
- Final post-fix APK installed and running on the connected Pixel.
- Local authenticated Courses flow passed through protected 19,778-byte material retrieval.
- Installed app correctly surfaces deployed Courses authentication failure and recovery.

Waiting:

- C1/C2 require the requested Luna review. Luna is unavailable in the current agent/model inventory and no local Luna executable exists. Terra-high review was used.
- Deployed Courses returns `503 notorganic_auth_adapter_unavailable`.
- Picture-in-picture obscures current device captures, so they do not establish look parity.

Completion blockers include native attachments and grounding recovery, complete settings, hosted wallet/token checkout, decks/SRS/profile, native Live, full course collaboration/offline conflicts, public sharing, iOS acceptance, desktop/TUI completion, and clean physical visual comparisons.

`vet` was invoked after each logical change but produced no verdict because it cannot reconstruct the large existing dirty-worktree diff (`DiffApplicationError`).

The mobile gap is now partially closed.

- Added a native [Usage & Study Activity page](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/usage.tsx:20), reachable from [More](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/more.tsx:21).
- It reports real local lessons, messages, attachments, artifacts, feedback, study topics, models, provider-reported tokens, and reported cost.
- It explicitly does not fabricate mastery. Quiz evidence, goals, SRS, retention, learner confidence, historical usage, and portable cross-platform records still require the shared learner repository.
- New replies now persist normalized provider/model/token usage. Older replies cannot retroactively recover missing token data.

The composer now supports images and documents through [Add images / Add documents](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/Composer.tsx:154), including validation, draft recovery, removal, transcript rendering, and provider-specific OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenRouter payloads. The Impeccable pass kept these controls compact and recoverable.

Verification:

- 123 mobile tests pass, 448 assertions.
- Strict TypeScript passes.
- Android export: 2,010 modules, 36 assets, 5.5 MB bundle.
- Release build: 946 Gradle tasks.
- Updated APK installed and launched on the connected Pixel.
- On-device verification confirmed the Usage page and attachment menu.
- I did not select a personal device file, so pick → preview → send remains unaccepted.
- Vet remains unverified because it crashes reconstructing the existing dirty worktree.

On self-augmentation:

- Mobile: no. It cannot rewrite its installed application or this repository.
- Normal web: can modify only its sandbox workspace.
- Locally hosted web with a project root and `--allow-local-exec`: can modify the actual checkout.
- TUI/Pi: yes. Its `edit`, `write`, and `bash` tools can change the working directory.
- `auto-improve`: changes policy and evolved-prompt artifacts; it does not automatically rewrite source code.

The host web and TUI mutation paths should gain an explicit preview/diff/confirmation/validation gate before being considered safe product behavior.

I updated the [build specification](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:118), [baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:54), and [execution checkpoint](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430). `/goal` remains active at 11.7% evidence-weighted completion: these additions do not yet satisfy the full M3 learner-data, Live, recovery, iOS, visual-parity, or required Luna-review gates.

You were right: Usage and study tracking were a major parity gap.

The mobile source now includes:

- A native [Usage & study activity page](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/usage.tsx:11) showing lessons, messages, attachments, saved items, feedback, studied topics, models, tokens, and provider-reported cost.
- SQLite-backed, restart-safe learner records with legacy migration.
- Serialized persistence at semantic boundaries such as completed messages, feedback, forks, and artifacts—not every streamed token.
- Honest provenance: lesson titles and artifacts count as study evidence, but do not fabricate mastery.

Still missing before genuine web parity: assessed mastery, goals, decks/SRS, Coming Up, historical charts, learner profile, and learner-facing import/export/delete controls.

On self-augmentation:

- Mobile currently cannot change its own code.
- Web can modify a disposable browser sandbox.
- Web can modify the actual project only when explicitly launched with `--host --allow-local-exec --root=...`.
- Pi/TUI may have local tooling, but OpenTUI lacks a proper capability, confirmation, diff, validation, and rollback experience.
- `auto-improve` evolves teaching policy/prompts; it is not source-code self-modification.

I added that distinction and its required safety gates to the [build plan](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:211), [execution program](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:553), and [parity baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:52).

Verification:

- Mobile: 132 tests, 482 assertions, strict typecheck passed.
- Shared learner contracts: 22 tests, 165 assertions, strict typecheck passed.
- Android export: 2,031 modules, 36 assets, 5.6 MB Hermes bundle.
- No Android device is currently connected, so this exact build is not installed/device-accepted.
- `vet` did not produce a trustworthy verdict—it previously crashed on the dirty diff and the latest run hung.
- `/goal` remains active at 11.7%; implementation advanced, but no additional full acceptance node has passed yet.

content.text:
F2 is complete in two new files only:

- `mobile/src/lib/learner-repository/portable-native-state.ts`
- `mobile/test/learner-portable-native-state.test.ts`

It provides:

- `projectPortableToNativeState(...)`
  - Preserves caller provider settings.
  - Restores only supplied app-owned attachment URIs; otherwise marks attachments `localState: "missing"`.
  - Applies latest exact feedback per message and counts all applicable feedback.
  - Preserves native-safe IDs, timestamps, and session lineage.
  - Explicitly reports unprojected session/artifact IDs and counts, including incompatible and ancestor-blocked sessions.
  - Refuses to flatten tool/system, noncanonical branch metadata, unknown providers, or unsupported artifact representations into lossy native equivalents.

- `reconcileNativeStateIntoPortable(...)`
  - Removes native-deleted projectable records.
  - Preserves imported-only goals/checks/quizzes/decks/reviews, unprojectable sessions/artifacts, needed ancestors, related records, learner strengths/weaknesses, and local attachment locations.
  - Revalidates final data through `validatePortableLearnerData`; reconciliation fails closed on dangling references.

Evidence:

- Focused test: 3 passing, 36 assertions.
- `mobile` strict typecheck: passed.
- Scoped `git diff --check`: passed.
- `rtk vet`: unverified; repeatable `DiffApplicationError` while applying the repository’s existing dirty diff.

content.text:
M3-U3 audit verdict: the portable store preserves learner records, but it cannot yet power a native dashboard or web-equivalent Coming Up loop.

Already available:

- Goals, question checks, quiz results, decks, card reviews, usage, feedback, and factual topic evidence have validated portable shapes.
- F2 projection/reconciliation correctly keeps unsupported/imported records outside the legacy native state instead of deleting them.
- `LearnerRecordStore` safely snapshots/replaces/imports/exports the complete portable envelope.

Missing contract capability:

1. Study priorities  
   There is no portable `StudyPriorityRecord`. Web Coming Up needs one canonical priority per `(targetType, targetId)`, with a durable update timestamp. Native needs targets for at least `deck`, `topic`, and an explicit pending-check/verification target.

2. Review scheduling  
   `FlashcardDeck.cards` has only front/back/tags; `CardReviewRecord` has historical interval/ease but no `dueAt` or current per-card SRS state. Therefore native cannot calculate due/overdue counts, next review, or support “Review this deck.” Add current card SRS state (`dueAt`, interval/ease/repetitions) and atomically update it with a review record.

3. Verification/check completion  
   Web Coming Up includes incomplete verifications. Portable artifacts have a `verification` kind but no completion state; question checks and quizzes are not an equivalent completion target. Add a typed verification/check record with `completedAt`/status, or add constrained verification status to artifacts.

4. Assessment revisions  
   `LearnerQuestionCheck` and `LearnerQuizResult` have only `createdAt`; grading alters a check without a mergeable update revision. Add `updatedAt` to mutable records, and enforce an explicit state rule such as pending checks having no final score. Preserve raw answer evidence and grading provenance.

5. Learner profile/dashboard derivation  
   The profile stores only explored topics, strengths, weaknesses, counts, and latest session. That is intentionally not mastery, but it cannot provide web’s topic profile / weak-concept queue. Add a derived, reproducible dashboard projection from assessments, reviews, and factual evidence—do not persist guessed mastery as source truth.

6. Typed repository mutations  
   The store exposes whole-snapshot replacement only. Dashboard actions need validated, exclusive, scoped mutations:

   - `upsert/deleteGoal`
   - `upsertQuestionCheck`, `gradeQuestionCheck`
   - `appendQuizResult`
   - `upsertDeck`
   - `recordCardReviewAndSchedule` (one transaction)
   - `setStudyPriority`
   - `completeVerification`
   - `dashboardSnapshot(now)` or a pure `buildLearnerDashboard(snapshot, now)`

   These must preserve unrelated imported records and validate the final portable graph before commit.

Native projection implications:

- Keep goals/assessments/decks/reviews/priorities out of `PersistedAppState`; native learner screens should read the portable repository directly.
- F2’s current unprojected accounting is correct for this. Reconciliation must retain all portable-only learning records, which it does today.
- Add a native `ComingUp` view model rather than trying to force these records into chat/session state.

Required invariants and tests:

- Exactly one priority per target; latest revision wins deterministically.
- A priority target must exist, except a learner-declared topic target.
- Every review references an existing deck/card; one atomic review updates both review history and current card schedule.
- Due/overdue ordering is deterministic for a supplied clock; old reviews cannot overwrite newer SRS state.
- Assessment grading has monotonic `updatedAt`; pending/final state combinations are valid only when explicitly supported.
- Topic evidence remains evidence, never a mastery claim; all referenced IDs remain valid after import, deletion, and reconciliation.
- Native deletion removes only projectable native records; imported goals/checks/quizzes/decks/reviews, unprojectable sessions/artifacts, needed ancestors, and linked evidence survive.
- Add force-kill/reopen tests for one completed quiz, a due card review, a priority change, and a verification completion; then physical offline device acceptance.

The primary parity blocker is concrete: web’s `buildComingUpQueue` requires deck-card `srs.dueAt`, incomplete verifications, learner priorities, and topic profiles. None are presently representable in `PortableLearnerData`, so native cannot honestly show the web queue yet.
I’m adding the pure learner-progress projection now. It will make the dashboard’s evidence boundaries explicit: activity, feedback, and learner notes never turn into inferred mastery.

Current terminal state:

| Area | Present | Missing for parity |
|---|---|---|
| Chat | Pi RPC transcript hydration, streaming, follow-up, abort, redacted failures, new session | Retry preserving a failed draft/session; session library/resume/rename/fork/import/export/share |
| Model/settings | Model and thinking cycling | Model catalog/search, provider/settings/capability view, availability reasons and recovery |
| Typed learner UI | Pi select/input/confirm/editor dialogs work; classic Pi has quiz widgets | OpenTUI’s `ui_document` path only calls `toolResultCardLines()` and appends static text. No answer, goal, deck, artifact, retry, or handoff action can be submitted or persisted |
| Learner evidence | Pi commands expose `/learner-state`, `/timeline`, `/due`, `/feedback` | No unified learner view, shared portable records, or terminal review controls |
| Artifacts/media | Static previews; classic Pi `/outputs` selector | Artifact library/actions; saved unknown documents; explicit terminal-safe media limitation and handoff (current image/scene text is not an actionable handoff) |
| Agent augmentation | Classic Pi may expose local tools; CLI has `edit` and improvement rollback paths | OpenTUI has no capability manifest, visible diff, explicit confirmation, validation/recovery, or snapshot rollback journey |
| Responsive/design | Activity rail hides below 100 cols; `/shell` works | 80×24-safe composition, green/paper semantic roles, 256/16-color and `NO_COLOR` handling, Unicode/ASCII fallback. `opentui-host.ts` hard-codes amber/dark hex values |

Important dependency finding: `@keating/learner-contracts` already provides the needed v1 semantic protocol: validated documents/actions/results, revision correlation, receipt journals, and idempotency-key collision protection. OpenTUI currently uses a separate legacy `src/tui/ui/types.ts` envelope and imports none of those shared contracts.
